sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: voice calls versus video calls, dictated versus typed texts, a held phone versus a mounted device, the warning period versus infractions, and extra guidance on children, friends and roadside scenes
Confusable pairs among the distracted driving and device rules, plus continuation facts that complete part C; each block ties to one guide page, the statute section number is a citation detail and is not taught, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec17-R01 | anchor: A02
A hands-free voice call is allowed while moving, but a video call is banned even when the phone is not held. [A02]
Why it matters: group device law; confusable voice call versus video call; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-R02 | anchor: A02
Text-based messages are allowed only through voice-to-text; typing or reading them by hand while moving is banned. [A02]
Why it matters: group device law; confusable dictated versus manual texting; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-R03 | anchor: A02
A rideshare driver may use a device to relay information through the company's network only if the device is attached or mounted to the vehicle. [A02]
Why it matters: group device law; confusable mounted versus held device; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-R04 | anchor: A02
The device bans listed in the law apply while the vehicle is in motion. [A02]
Why it matters: group device law; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-R05 | anchor: A02
Since January 1, 2025, a device law violation may be treated as an infraction rather than only a warning. [A02]
Why it matters: group device law; confusable warning period versus infraction; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-R06 | anchor: A02
Disqualification is a possible consequence named only for commercial drivers who violate the device law. [A02]
Why it matters: group device law; confusable commercial versus noncommercial consequences; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-R07 | anchor: A02
Stay focused on driving and remain alert so you reach your destination safely, instead of studying the scenery you pass. [A02]
Why it matters: group roadside distractions; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-R08 | anchor: A01
Teach young children that driving is an important job that needs your concentration when you are behind the wheel. [A01]
Why it matters: group passengers; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec17-R09 | anchor: A01
A car full of friends can distract you with loud talk, arguments over music, or horseplay. [A01]
Why it matters: group passengers; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec17-R10 | anchor: A01
A loose pet in a moving vehicle can be very dangerous. [A01]
Why it matters: group pets; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec17-R11 | anchor: A01
Talking with passengers appears on the guide's list of distractions, alongside eating, grooming and reading. [A01]
Why it matters: group distractions; confusable ordinary activities as distractions; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec17-R12 | anchor: A01
Under the heading turning dials can turn your head, the guide warns that working in-vehicle controls pulls your attention from the road. [A01]
Why it matters: group in-vehicle controls; mnemonic heading.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]
